Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New 2025</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;padding-left:18pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.5pt">Third quarter 2026 reported and adjusted diluted EPS were $2.23 and $2.28, compared with $2.61 and $2.75 in the third quarter 2025</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;padding-left:18pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.5pt">Adjusting full-year guidance for reported diluted EPS to be in the range of $8.04 to $8.49 and adjusted diluted EPS to be in the range of $9.25 to $9.70</font></div><div style="text-indent:-4.5pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="margin-top:12pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">WESTCHESTER, Ill., November&#160;5, 2026</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> &#8211; Ingredion Incorporated (NYSE&#58; INGR), a leading global provider of ingredient solutions to the food and beverage manufacturing industry, today reported its third quarter 2026 results.</font></div><div style="margin-top:12pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8220;Our third quarter results fell short of our expectations, largely due to Argo&#8217;s slower than anticipated financial recovery, with incremental pressure from higher input costs and consumer softness,&#8221; said Jim Zallie, chairman, president and CEO of Ingredion. &#8220;While production at Argo remained stable for a second consecutive quarter and inventories are largely rebuilt, high manufacturing costs coupled with softer food and beverage demand impacted profitable volume growth. With plant reliability improved, our focus has shifted to sustainably lowering operating costs and improving volume growth. While we expect these actions to improve earnings, the recovery is taking longer than we expected.&#8221;</font></div><div style="margin-top:12pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8220;For Texture and Healthful Solutions, net sales volume growth was a bright spot again this quarter. Volume grew for the tenth consecutive quarter, supported by continued strong demand for clean label globally as customers reformulate for simpler labels, affordability and nutrition. However, higher tapioca costs and manufacturing input cost inflation negatively impacted profit growth in the segment. In Food &#38; Industrial Ingredients&#8212;LATAM, stronger volume from brewing and beverage customers in Mexico and Brazil was offset by foreign exchange impacts from a stronger Mexican peso and the impact to our Andean operations from the August earthquake in Colombia.&#8221; </font></div><div style="margin-top:12pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8220;As a result, we are lowering our full-year outlook, primarily to reflect the slower earnings recovery in Food &#38; Industrial Ingredients&#8212;U.S.&#47;CAN, along with the impacts of higher input costs and softer demand.&#8221;</font></div><div style="margin-top:12pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8220;Looking ahead, we are taking action to improve financial performance through operating cost discipline and spend management, while we continue to invest in our specialty growth platforms. As we progress the integration planning for the pending acquisition of Tate &#38; Lyle, we are building the foundation for an even stronger company with greater opportunities for growth, innovation and shareholder value creation in 2027 and beyond.&#8221;</font></div><div style="height:72pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">*</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:14pt">Reported results are in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles &#8220;GAAP.&#8221; Adjusted financial measures are non-GAAP financial measures. See &#8220;II. Non-GAAP Information&#8221; in the Supplemental Financial Information that follows the Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements for a reconciliation of non-GAAP financial measures to the most sale of the majority stake in our Pakistan business partially offset by continued improvements in the Protein Fortification business.</font></div><div style="margin-top:12pt;padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-13.5pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">**   All Other consists of the businesses of multiple operating segments that are not individually or collectively classified as reportable segments. Net sales from All Other are generated primarily by sales of stevia and other ingredients from our PureCircle and other sugar reduction businesses, and pea protein ingredients from our Protein Fortification business.</font></div><div style="margin-top:12pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Other Financial Items</font></div><div style="margin-top:3pt;padding-left:18pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:15.2pt">At September&#160;30, 2026, total debt was $1.8 billion, and cash, including short-term investments, was $993 million, versus $1.8 billion and $1.0 billion at December&#160;31, 2025.</font></div><div style="margin-top:3pt;padding-left:18pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.5pt">Net adjusted financing costs were $10 million in third quarter 2026, compared to $7 million in third quarter 2025.</font></div><div style="margin-top:3pt;padding-left:18pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.5pt">Reported and adjusted effective tax rates for the third quarter were 26.8% and 26.4%, respectively, compared to 28.6% and 26.4%, respectively, for the year-ago period. The decrease in the reported effective tax rate was primarily driven by the change in the permanent reinvestment status of our Pakistan business recorded in the prior-year period and a favorable ruling in Brazil related to the taxability of ICMS credits. These favorable impacts were partially offset by the change in the value of the Mexican peso relative to the U.S. dollar.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:0.1pt;margin-top:3pt;padding-left:18pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.5pt">Capital expenditures totaled $313 million through September&#160;30, 2026, partially offset by proceeds of $36 million from the sales of certain properties.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:0.1pt;margin-top:12pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Dividends and Share Repurchases</font></div><div style="margin-top:12pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">In the third quarter, the Company paid $53 million in dividends to shareholders. On September&#160;17, 2026, the Company declared a quarterly dividend increase to $0.83 per share, which was paid on October&#160;20, 2026, marking the 12</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:6.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-3.5pt;vertical-align:baseline">th </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">consecutive year of dividend increases. Through September 30, the Company repurchased $85 million of common stock and is on track to complete its $100 million full-year share repurchase target.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:0.1pt;margin-top:12pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Updated Full-Year 2026 Outlook</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:0.1pt;margin-top:12pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The Company now expects its full-year 2026 reported diluted EPS to be in the range of $8.04 to $8.49, and its adjusted diluted EPS to be in the range of $9.25 to $9.70.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:0.1pt;margin-top:12pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The Company now expects full-year 2026 net sales to be flat, reflecting volume growth and favorable foreign exchange, offset by lower price mix as well as the impact of the previously mentioned sale of its majority stake in the Pakistan business. Excluding results of the Pakistan business, net sales is expected to be flat to up low single digits.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:0.1pt;margin-top:12pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Reported operating income is expected to be down low double digits, with adjusted operating income now expected to be down mid-teens for full-year 2026, which reflects the operational challenges in F&#38;II</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'null',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8211;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">U.S.&#47;CAN.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:0.1pt;margin-top:12pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The 2026 full-year outlook further assumes the following&#58; Texture &#38; Healthful Solutions operating income is now expected to be flat to up low single-digits, driven by sales volume growth, offset by expected higher input cost inflation&#59; Food &#38; Industrial Ingredients</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'null',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8211;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">LATAM operating income is now anticipated to be down mid-to-high single-digits, reflecting the continued strength of the Mexican peso&#59; Food &#38; Industrial Ingredients</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'null',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8211;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">U.S.&#47;CAN operating income is now expected to be down 35-40%, driven by operating costs at Argo&#59; and All Other&#8217;s operating loss is still anticipated to be approximately $(15) million, which reflects the absence of a second half earnings contribution from the sale of the  Pakistan business. </font></div><div style="height:72pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:0.1pt;margin-top:12pt"><font><br></font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:45pt;width:100%"><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">INGREDION REPORTS THIRD QUARTER 2026 RESULTS &#8211; In addition, this guidance excludes acquisition-related integration and restructuring costs, as well as any potential impairment costs.</font></div><div style="margin-top:12pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Conference Call and Webcast Details</font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:112%">Ingredion will host a conference call on Thursday, November&#160;5, 2026, at 8 a.m. CT&#47;9 a.m. ET, hosted by Jim Zallie, chairman, president and chief executive officer and Diego Reynoso, executive vice president and chief financial officer. With 2025 annual net sales of approximately $7.2 billion, the Company turns grains, fruits, vegetables and other plant-based materials into value-added ingredient solutions for the food, beverage, animal nutrition, brewing and industrial markets. With Ingredion Idea Labs</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:6.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-3.5pt;vertical-align:baseline">&#174;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> innovation centers located around the world and more than 11,000 employees, the Company co-creates with customers and fulfills its purpose of bringing the potential of people, nature and technology together to make life better. Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">II. Non-GAAP Information</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:0.1pt;margin-top:12pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">To supplement the consolidated financial results prepared in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (&#8220;GAAP&#8221;), non-GAAP historical financial measures are used, which exclude certain GAAP items such as acquisition&#47;integration costs, restructuring costs, impairment charges, net (gain) on sale of business, Mexico tax item, and other specified items. The term &#8220;adjusted&#8221; is generally used when referring to these non-GAAP financial measures.</font></div><div style="margin-top:12pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Management uses non-GAAP financial measures internally for strategic decision making, forecasting future results and evaluating current performance. By disclosing non-GAAP financial measures, management intends to provide investors with a more meaningful, consistent comparison of the Company&#8217;s operating results and trends for the periods presented. These non-GAAP financial measures are used in addition to and in conjunction with results presented in accordance with GAAP and reflect an additional way of viewing aspects of the Company&#8217;s operations that, when viewed with its GAAP results, provide a more complete understanding of factors and trends affecting its business. Expected financial measures may not reflect certain future charges, costs and&#47;or gains that are inherently difficult to predict and estimate due to their unknown timing, effect and&#47;or significance. Non-GAAP adjustments are generally made to adjusted financial measures, which increases management&#8217;s confidence in its ability to forecast adjusted financial measures than in its ability to forecast GAAP financial measures. These non-GAAP measures, including non-GAAP expected measures, should be considered as a supplement to, and not as a substitute for, or superior to, the corresponding measures calculated in accordance with GAAP.</font></div><div style="margin-top:12pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Non-GAAP financial measures are not prepared in accordance with GAAP&#59; therefore, the Company&#8217;s non-GAAP information is not necessarily comparable to similarly titled measures presented by other companies. A reconciliation of each non-GAAP financial measure to the most comparable GAAP measure is provided in the tables below.</font></div><div Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:8.57pt">During the three and nine months ended September&#160;30, 2026, we recorded net pre-tax acquisition and integration costs of  $6&#160;million and $59 million primarily related to our pending acquisition of Tate &#38; Lyle, including $5 million and $42&#160;million of gains and losses of acquisition-related foreign exchange hedging for the three and nine months ended September&#160;30, 2026. There was no such activity during the three and nine months ended September&#160;30, 2025.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;padding-left:18pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">(ii)</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:5.8pt">During the three and nine months ended September&#160;30, 2026, we recorded pre-tax impairment charges of $6 million and $39 million. In the third quarter we recorded a charge related to the sale of our facility in Vanscoy, Canada and impairment charge on an equity investment. In addition, we recorded charges relating to the closure our Cabo, Brazil facility in the first half of 2026. During the nine months ended September&#160;30, 2025, we recorded $6&#160;million of pre-tax impairment charges on our equity investments.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;padding-left:18pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">(iii)</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:3.03pt">During the three and nine months ended September&#160;30, 2026, we recorded a pre-tax restructuring benefit of $17&#160;million and pre-tax restructuring charges of $8 million. The benefit during the quarter was primarily from the gain on the sale of land in Lane Cove, Australia. During the nine months ended September&#160;30, 2026, the gain on sale of land was fully offset by restructuring costs primarily related to the closure of our facility in Cabo, Brazil and the sale of our Pakistan business. During the three and nine months ended September&#160;30, 2025, we recorded pre-tax restructuring costs of $3&#160;million and $7&#160;million, primarily related to decommissioning costs for plant closures.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;padding-left:18pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">(iv)</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:3.57pt">During the nine months ended September&#160;30, 2026, we recorded a net pre-tax gain of $44&#160;million related to the sale of our Pakistan business. There was no such activity during September&#160;30, 2025.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;padding-left:18pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">(v)</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:6.34pt">During the three and nine months ended September&#160;30, 2026, we recorded pre-tax charges of $8 million and $25&#160;million primarily related to the Argo thermal event. During the three and nine months ended September&#160;30, 2025, we recorded pre-tax expenses of $2&#160;million and pre-tax benefits of $9&#160;million primarily related to insurance recoveries and a favorable judgment related to certain indirect taxes. </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;padding-left:18pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">(vi)</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:3.57pt">The tax amounts are result of the movement of the Mexican peso against the U.S. dollar and its impact on the remeasurement of the Mexico financial statements during the period.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;padding-left:18pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">(vii)</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:0.8pt">During the three and nine months ended September&#160;30, 2026, we recognized tax benefits, including interest income associated with certain Brazilian local incentives and the recognition of a U.S. deferred tax asset. These benefits were partially offset by the related tax impacts of current- and prior-year non-GAAP adjustments and the recapture of prior-year U.S. tax benefits. Additionally, during the nine months ended September 30, 2026, we recognized tax benefits associated with the utilization of previously unbenefited capital losses. These benefits were partially offset by changes in our accrual related to the permanent reinvestment of foreign earnings and the recognition of prior-year tax liabilities.</font></div><div style="height:45pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:0.1pt;margin-top:12pt"><font><br></font></div></div></div><div id="if61284571e884eac8eb2d415b2a488f8_22"></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:45pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:0.1pt;margin-top:12pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">II.
